ActionAvailability.description:
Whether one action is currently safe -- decided by the reducer, never the UI.

``disabledReason`` and ``nextSafeAction`` are load-bearing for slice 06: the
cockpit renders the affordance and its tooltip straight from this and never
infers safety client-side.
ActionAvailability.title: ActionAvailability

Analytics.description:
The slice-3b analytical surfaces: charts/feeds for specific cockpit panels.

Kept apart from the structural task/enclosure/provider tree so the
client-agnostic core stays small. Large raw inventories are deliberately *not*
here -- drift rows stay in the snapshot file, the full sidecar list collapses to
the histogram + a bounded leaderboard -- so the served projection stays lean.

``attentionQueue`` (slice 05) and ``engineProcesses`` (slice 5e) are the *derived*
surfaces here: the reducer composes them from the structural tree + these signals (not
from an input file), so a structural-only caller can still see them populated.
Analytics.title: Analytics

AttentionItem.description:
One thing that needs the human, decided by the reducer (note 06, slice 05).

A ranked cross-section of the structural tree + analytics signals -- the
home-screen attention queue. Computed server-side so every client (dashboard,
TUI, agent) shares one queue, and ``waitSeconds`` is a server-computed age, never
a client's render time. The ``*Id`` / ``enclosure`` cross-refs point back into the
structural tree so the UI can couple a queue item to its operation-tree node.
AttentionItem.title: AttentionItem

CloseoutCandidateNode.description: One exact-current member of the disposable scheduling projection.
CloseoutCandidateNode.title: CloseoutCandidateNode

CloseoutProjectionProblemNode.description: Bounded repair evidence for a non-admitting projection.
CloseoutProjectionProblemNode.title: CloseoutProjectionProblemNode

CloseoutQueueNode.description: Exact effective state for one disposable sprint scheduling projection.
CloseoutQueueNode.title: CloseoutQueueNode

CommitRefNode.description:
One side of the official-line/worktree pair: a branch @ commit at a path (slice 5e).

``factState`` is the honesty axis: ``observed`` means the worktree checkout exists on
disk; ``derived`` means the value is a recorded contract field whose checkout is not
present; ``planned`` is an expected-but-not-yet step; ``missing`` is unobservable; and
``not-applicable`` is a lane that does not exist (e.g. memory on a ``disabled`` contract).
The cockpit colours/animates from this so it never renders a planned path as a live one.
CommitRefNode.title: CommitRefNode

DirectGrantNode.description:
A leaf's direct-execution grant as the dashboard shows it (MIK-R94 rule 4).

Read from the one grant record at projection time, never stored twice.
``None`` on the parent node distinguishes a leaf with no grant.
DirectGrantNode.title: DirectGrantNode

DiscardUnstartedProofNode.description: Persisted proof facts retained after an unstarted leaf source is discarded.
DiscardUnstartedProofNode.title: DiscardUnstartedProofNode

DiscardedSubTaskNode.description: One master-owned, machine-readable discard-unstarted audit entry.
DiscardedSubTaskNode.title: DiscardedSubTaskNode

DriftSnapshotNode.description:
A repo's onboarding-drift result, read from a persisted JSON snapshot (3b, b1).

The reducer never classifies drift (that is git-per-sidecar -- far too costly for
a poll-cadence write); it reads the snapshot the memory_quality drift run
persisted and surfaces ``snapshotStaleSeconds`` (age of ``checkedAt``), exactly
like a provider tile. The full per-sidecar rows stay in the snapshot file; the
projection carries only the classification counts a gauge needs.
DriftSnapshotNode.title: DriftSnapshotNode

EnclosureNode.description:
A worktree enclosure (contract + group): the persistent identity anchor.

``lifecycleId`` is the contract's operation-binding key. It is not a
separately projected agent session or a source of task activity.

``codeWorktreeExists`` / ``memoryWorktreeExists`` are the worktree-existence
TRUTH (L11): stat'ed at snapshot time in the I/O layer, exactly how the worktree
tools report existence (``contract.code_worktree.exists()`` in
``worktree_status``). The tasks surface filters visibility on these, never on a
cleanup-state proxy — ``cleanup: reopened`` means contract-reset-awaiting-restart
(worktrees gone until the next ``worktree_start``), not live work.
EnclosureNode.title: EnclosureNode

EngineProcessEdge.description:
One conduit in the process map, with a state-backed visual treatment (slice 5e).

Edges are derived from facts, never decoration: a ``cgc-seed`` edge reads ``running``
only while the seed phase is live, ``failed`` on a failed phase, ``planned`` before it
starts -- so an animated conduit always means an observed transition.
EngineProcessEdge.title: EngineProcessEdge

EngineProcessNode.description:
One worktree enclosure as a state-backed process -- the Engine Room's unit (slice 5e).

Composed (like ``attentionQueue``) from the contract + status guidance + provider boot +
lifecycle, **not** read from a new file. The center of the Engine Room is this enclosure,
not a provider card: the official source line, the code/memory worktrees, the contract
coupling them, and the two isolated engines bound to that worktree group. ``health`` and
the per-side ``factState``s carry the observed/derived/planned/missing honesty 5e demands.
EngineProcessNode.title: EngineProcessNode

LandingRefNode.description:
One remote/PR participant in the successful-landing arc (slice 5h).

The landing tail references refs the *worktree* projection has no node for -- ``origin/main``,
``origin/<feat>``, the PR, ``origin/mem-main``. Like :class:`CommitRefNode`, ``factState`` is the
honesty axis so the cockpit never animates a *planned* PR as an observed one: ``observed`` means a
live probe (``git ls-remote`` / ``gh``) confirmed it, ``planned`` is an expected-but-not-yet step,
and ``missing`` is a probe that could not run (e.g. ``gh`` absent/unauthed).
LandingRefNode.title: LandingRefNode

LedgerNode.description:
A repo's memory ledger currency (slice 3b, surface 8).

``closeoutCount`` is the ledger row count (one row per closeout); the rows carry
no timestamps, so "closeouts over time" is deliberately not projected -- only the
count + the last-verified-code-commit currency.

``rows`` is the newest ``LEDGER_WINDOW`` code<->memory mappings for the OFFICIAL coupler
popover (5h); ``closeoutCount`` stays the full total so the popover's "+N more" footer is right.
LedgerNode.title: LedgerNode

LedgerRefNode.description:
One memory.md ledger row -- a code-commit -> memory-commit mapping (5h coupler popover).

The warp couplers stand for the memory.md ledger link; the popover renders a window of these
rows with this enclosure's row highlighted. Full SHAs (the popover shortens them for display).

The optional ``*Subject`` / ``*Date`` fields are the per-side commit message + committer ISO
date, probed best-effort from the local repos in the snapshots I/O layer (5h Tier 2: "hashes
alone don't tell a story"). They are ``None`` -- and, since the projection dumps
``exclude_none=True``, omitted from the wire -- when the commit is not in the local repo or the
git probe could not run, so the popover row honestly falls back to the hash alone. Never faked.
LedgerRefNode.title: LedgerRefNode

LifecycleApprovalObservation.description: Approval claim read from the same exact journal revision.
LifecycleApprovalObservation.title: LifecycleApprovalObservation

LifecycleOperationProjection.description: One coherent, task-addressed lifecycle journal observation.
LifecycleOperationProjection.title: LifecycleOperationProjection

LifecycleProjectionComponentBindings.description: Identity digest claimed by every optional nested projection component.
LifecycleProjectionComponentBindings.title: LifecycleProjectionComponentBindings

LifecycleProjectionIdentity.description: One exact journal snapshot and its admitted candidate/plan.
LifecycleProjectionIdentity.title: LifecycleProjectionIdentity

LifecycleRecommendedAction.description: Required recovery edge, distinct from optional legal controls.
LifecycleRecommendedAction.title: LifecycleRecommendedAction

LifecycleWorkerObservation.description: Public liveness class without exposing process or lease authority.
LifecycleWorkerObservation.title: LifecycleWorkerObservation

Metrics.description: Workspace verification-age distribution; task counts belong to task entries.
Metrics.title: Metrics

ProviderBootNode.description:
One isolated engine in a worktree's provider runtime: CGC (code) or GrepAI (memory).

The boot *sequence* (seed/clone/watcher phases) lives on the owning
:class:`EngineProcessNode` because provider setup is one progress file per worktree
group; this node is the engine's identity + its current runtime health.
ProviderBootNode.title: ProviderBootNode

ProviderNode.description:
One provider's current-state snapshot (data surfaces 1 and 4).

``snapshotStaleSeconds`` is the age of the ``current.json`` file: provider
state is call-triggered and stale between calls, so the reducer surfaces how
old the snapshot is rather than pretending it is live. Workspace providers
can be aggregate nodes or repo-covered nodes when the provider snapshot
carries per-repo evidence. Worktree providers carry ``worktreeGroup`` and
bind to their isolated enclosure.
ProviderNode.title: ProviderNode

RouteCoverageNode.description: One onboarding route's coverage, from its ``overview.index.json`` (3b, surface 10).
RouteCoverageNode.title: RouteCoverageNode

SetupProgressNode.description:
A worktree group's live provider-setup progress (slice 3b, surface 3).

Projected through ``setup_progress.progress_status``, so a ``running`` group
whose heartbeat went stale reads ``stale`` -- the boot-sequence widget data.
SetupProgressNode.title: SetupProgressNode

SetupSummaryNode.description: The latest provider-setup outcome for one action (slice 3b, surface 2).
SetupSummaryNode.title: SetupSummaryNode

SidecarStaleNode.description:
One onboarding sidecar's verification age (slice 3b, surface 11; git-free).

Read from the sidecar's table metadata (``lastVerifiedCommitDate``) with no git
-- the always-on complement to the drift snapshot. The projection carries only
the *stalest* bounded sample (a leaderboard); the full distribution is the
``Metrics.stalenessHistogram`` rollup.
SidecarStaleNode.title: SidecarStaleNode

SourceLineageEdge.description: One plane-resolved ancestry edge; agents never supply or retain commit ids.
SourceLineageEdge.title: SourceLineageEdge

SourceLineageProjection.description: Transitive super -> master -> leaf lineage projected into status and refusals.
SourceLineageProjection.title: SourceLineageProjection

SourceLineageRecovery.description: One ordered recovery derived from task identity, not model-carried Git state.
SourceLineageRecovery.title: SourceLineageRecovery

TaskCodeExampleNode.description: One proposed-code-example block of a task document (the plan's distinct change shapes).
TaskCodeExampleNode.title: TaskCodeExampleNode

TaskDecisionNode.description: One decision-log row of a task document.
TaskDecisionNode.title: TaskDecisionNode

TaskDependencyNode.description: A direct same-master dependency, including a no-longer-listed task.
TaskDependencyNode.title: TaskDependencyNode

TaskDocumentRef.description: Address of one task document: the ``repository`` id plus the document ``path`` inside that repository's task root.
TaskDocumentRef.title: TaskDocumentRef

TaskEntry.description: One qualified task, its authored summary, runtime facts and ordered children.
TaskEntry.title: TaskEntry

TaskExecutionEdgeNode.description: One reasoned dependency edge in a sprint task document.
TaskExecutionEdgeNode.title: TaskExecutionEdgeNode

TaskExecutionEndpointNode.description:
One resolved-form edge endpoint: the master ref plus the segment-sampling leaf id.

The persisted grammar also allows a bare ref (lump/legacy); the before-validator
lifts that form so the served shape is uniform.
TaskExecutionEndpointNode.title: TaskExecutionEndpointNode

TaskExecutionGraphNode.description: Persisted AON graph projected without adding scheduler judgment.
TaskExecutionGraphNode.title: TaskExecutionGraphNode

TaskExecutionGraphView.description:
The render-ready sprint graph, ordered by derived wave then node order.

Nodes within a wave keep the persisted declaration order, so a re-render
with an unchanged graph is byte-stable.
TaskExecutionGraphView.title: TaskExecutionGraphView

TaskExecutionNode.description: One graph node: a whole-master lump or a leaf-segment of one master (L11-R1).
TaskExecutionNode.title: TaskExecutionNode

TaskExecutionNodeView.description:
Render-ready per-node sprint graph model (L12-R4).

``nodeId`` is a stable semantic identity: a lump's master ref key, or the
ref key plus a segment ordinal for a segmented master. ``waveIndex`` is the
1-based derived wave; ``frontierState`` is derived mechanically from task
statuses and the graph edges -- the dashboard styles, never re-derives.
TaskExecutionNodeView.title: TaskExecutionNodeView

TaskExecutionPredecessorNode.description: One predecessor edge of a projected graph node with its recorded reason.
TaskExecutionPredecessorNode.title: TaskExecutionPredecessorNode

TaskHeaderNoteNode.description:
One extra header metadata line of a task document (MIK-R127 rule 9).

Rendered as ``label: value`` in the head strip; at most six on the page, with a
link to all where there are more.
TaskHeaderNoteNode.title: TaskHeaderNoteNode

TaskIntentIdentity.description: Canonical task-intent schema plus its exact projection digest.
TaskIntentIdentity.title: TaskIntentIdentity

TaskReviewFindingNode.description:
One review finding of a task document (MIK-R127 rule 9).

Every baseline finding is projected with its open flag: the Review block
draws the open ones, and the findings view draws the whole round.
TaskReviewFindingNode.title: TaskReviewFindingNode

TaskReviewStateNode.description:
The review round of a task document (MIK-R127 rule 9), bounded as shown.

``findings`` carries the round's baseline findings with their descriptions
(what the Review block and the findings view draw); ``totalFindings`` names
the whole round for the link, and ``openFindings`` counts the open ones of
the whole round: a summary carries only the first findings, so a reader
must not count their open flags for the round.
TaskReviewStateNode.title: TaskReviewStateNode

TaskSeatNode.description:
One first-class seat of an orchestration sprint (L14-R3).

Mirrors ``tasks.document.SprintSeat``: the sprint document owns the seat record, so seat task
documents leave the sprint's task index (existing ones stay on disk as historical records).
``identity`` is a correlatable session or catalog id — provenance for correlation, never an
authority source.
TaskSeatNode.title: TaskSeatNode

TaskSectionNode.description:
One ordered section of a master's render plan: freeform prose or a generated block (6g).

Mirrors ``tasks.document.Section`` so the master overview renders its bespoke sections in order.
TaskSectionNode.title: TaskSectionNode

TaskStepDispositionNode.description: Why and when one exact task work unit was intentionally skipped.
TaskStepDispositionNode.title: TaskStepDispositionNode

TaskStepNode.description:
One step of a task document, with its substeps -- the actual task *content* (slice 5c).

The 3c projection carried only step counts; the cockpit detail needs the step list itself to
show what a lifecycle is actually doing, so the served node carries the titles + statuses.
TaskStepNode.title: TaskStepNode

TaskSubStepNode.description: One substep of a task step (the JSON's finer-grained progress unit).
TaskSubStepNode.title: TaskSubStepNode

TaskSummary.description:
A task document's progress and reader content (slice 3c, surface 7).

Read from the JSON-primary ``ar-task-document/v1`` document, so the dashboard
can show authored task facts without opening files on disk. Planning documents
are projected before an enclosure exists.
TaskSummary.title: TaskSummary

ToolReportNode.description: A recent verbose tool-report file (slice 3b, surface 12; bounded keep-last-5).
ToolReportNode.title: ToolReportNode
